briefdescription.para: Refuse a particle the section cannot integrate; nothing to check for the Cartesian section.

detaileddescription.para:
An axisymmetric particle is refused with a vertex at $ r < 0 $ (beyond the round-off of a mesher, relative to the diagonal of the bounding box), or with smoothing domains that do not tile the body (any update of the smoothing domain but DeformationGradient): the integration constraint needs them. It may touch the axis with a vertex or a face: the ring weight vanishes there, and its center has $ \bar r > 0 $.

memberdef.name: addPressure

briefdescription.para: Add the follower pressure on one face of a particle to its external force, and its tangent.

detaileddescription.para:
With the face rule of the smoothing (faceQuadrature()), each point $ \boldsymbol{Y}_g $ of the face carries the force of Nanson's formula in the plane of the section, from $ \boldsymbol{Y} $ to $ \boldsymbol{x} $, times the weight of the section after the increment, \[ \boldsymbol{f}_g = -\Delta J\, \Delta\boldsymbol{F}^{-\mathsf{T}}\, p\, \frac{\boldsymbol{n}_f\,dA_f}{n_g}\; w_g , \qquad f_{Ai} \mathrel{-}= \sum_g T_A(\boldsymbol{Y}_g)\, f_{g,i} , \] with $ w_g = 1 $ (Cartesian) or the ring of the point after the increment, $ w_g = 2\pi x_r(\boldsymbol{Y}_g) $ (Hoop::ringOfFacePoint()): the face moves with the motion of the particle, and its ring grows with the hoop stretch of the point. As for the elements, a positive pressure pushes on the face (against the outward normal). The tangent differentiates $ \Delta\boldsymbol{F} $ (through $ \tilde N_{B,L} $) and, axisymmetric, $ w_g $ (Hoop::dRingOfFacePoint_dDeltaq_Br()). For a uniform stress, the pressure $ -\sigma_{nn} $ on the boundary balances the internal force of a linear field exactly, because the face rule is that of the integration constraint.

The number of dofs per node; the displacement comes first.

The material point of the particle.

The face in the intermediate configuration.

The pressure.
materialPoint
The material point at the center, evaluated for the increment: its $ \Delta\boldsymbol{F} $ in the plane of the section, and (axisymmetric) its $ \Delta F_{\theta\theta} $ and its position, the particle center $ \bar{\boldsymbol{Y}} $.
N
The trial functions at the center, 1 x nNodes.

Their smoothed gradients, nDim x nNodes.

The meshfree approximation, for the test functions at the points.

The kernel functions of the nodes.

The external force, node-wise.
dFExt_ddQ
Its tangent, column-major; nullptr for none (explicit).

briefdescription.para: The integrals over the smoothing domain of a particle in its section: its volume, the smoothed gradients of the shape functions (stabilized conforming nodal integration, Chen et al., 2001), its second moments and the face loads.

detaileddescription.para: The notation is that of the page "Meshfree Particles": $ N_{A,i} = \partial N_A / \partial Y_i $ with the coordinates $ \boldsymbol{Y} $ of the intermediate configuration, the volume $ |\Omega_s| $ of the smoothing domain $ \Omega_s $ (volume()), and the area vector $ n_{f,i}\,dA_f $ of its face $ f $ (LagrangeCell::boundarySurfaceVector()). In 2D, $ dA_f $ is the length of the face (the area of unit thickness in plane strain).

The smoothed gradient is the average of the gradient over $ \Omega_s $, turned into a boundary integral by the divergence theorem and integrated with a rule on each face (faceQuadrature()). In the Cartesian section (plane strain, 3D) the rule is one point per face, the face center $ \boldsymbol{Y}_f $, \[ \tilde N_{A,i} = \frac{1}{|\Omega_s|}\int_{\Omega_s} N_{A,i}\,dV = \frac{1}{|\Omega_s|}\oint_{\partial\Omega_s} N_A\,n_i\,dA \approx \frac{1}{|\Omega_s|} \sum_f N_A(\boldsymbol{Y}_f)\, n_{f,i}\, dA_f . \] Here the face rule is the only approximation, and only the values of the shape functions at the face points are needed. NSNI smooths the second derivatives alike, from the (unsmoothed) gradients at the same points, \[ \hat N_{A,IJ} = \frac{1}{|\Omega_s|} \sum_f N_{A,I}(\boldsymbol{Y}_f)\, n_{f,J}\, dA_f , \] stored unsymmetrized as d2N_dYdY[J](I, A); NSNI::secondGradientOfNode() symmetrizes them.

In the axisymmetric section, $ \Omega_s $ is the ring swept by the smoothing domain of the meridian half plane $ (r, z) = (Y_1, Y_2) $ (Y( 0 ) is $ r $ in the code), and every integral carries the ring weight $ 2\pi r $ (weight()): $ |\Omega_s| = 2\pi A_s \bar r $, with the area $ A_s $ and the radius $ \bar r $ of the area centroid $ \bar{\boldsymbol{Y}} $ of the smoothing domain (the particle center). The divergence theorem of the weighted gradient gains an area term, $ r N_{A,r} = (r N_A)_{,r} - N_A $, which is integrated with the centroid; the faces are integrated with two Gauss points $ \boldsymbol{Y}_g $ each, which share $ n_{f,i}\,dA_f $ equally: \[ \tilde N_{A,i} = \frac{1}{|\Omega_s|} \sum_f \sum_{g=1}^{2} 2\pi r_g\, N_A(\boldsymbol{Y}_g)\, \frac{n_{f,i}\, dA_f}{2} - \delta_{ir}\, \frac{N_A(\bar{\boldsymbol{Y}})}{\bar r} . \] The hoop operator $ \tilde H_A = N_A(\bar{\boldsymbol{Y}}) / \bar r $ (in Hoop::force() and Hoop::addStiffnessOfNode()) is the ring average of $ N_A / r $ with the same area integral. Together they satisfy the integration constraint of the ring, the discrete divergence theorem of the 3D field $ N_A \boldsymbol{e}_r $, whose divergence is $ N_{A,r} + N_A / r $: for every smoothing domain, \[ |\Omega_s| \bigl(\tilde N_{A,r} + \tilde H_A\bigr) = \sum_f \sum_{g=1}^{2} 2\pi r_g\, N_A(\boldsymbol{Y}_g)\, \frac{n_{f,r}\, dA_f}{2} , \qquad |\Omega_s|\, \tilde N_{A,z} = \sum_f \sum_{g=1}^{2} 2\pi r_g\, N_A(\boldsymbol{Y}_g)\, \frac{n_{f,z}\, dA_f}{2} , \] the area terms cancelling within the smoothing domain. Summed over smoothing domains that tile the body, the face sums of the shared faces cancel, and what remains is the face sum over the boundary of the body. A face on the axis has $ r_g = 0 $ and drops out: the axis is no boundary of the body of revolution. A face load is integrated with the same rule (addPressure()), so that the load $ \boldsymbol{\sigma}\,\boldsymbol{n} $ of a uniform stress balances the internal force of a linear field exactly. The second derivatives of NSNI are smoothed alike, \[ \hat N_{A,IJ} = \frac{1}{|\Omega_s|} \sum_f \sum_{g=1}^{2} 2\pi \Big( r_g\, N_{A,I}(\boldsymbol{Y}_g)\, n_{f,J} - \delta_{Jr}\, N_A(\boldsymbol{Y}_g)\, n_{f,I} \Big) \frac{dA_f}{2} , \] and the second moments are those of the ring about the area centroid, $ 2\pi \int \boldsymbol{\xi} \otimes \boldsymbol{\xi}\, r\, dA $.

The particles take these integrals and their evaluation points (faceQuadraturePoints()) from here and not from the cell: the face rule of the smoothing is defined in this class only. So do the SQCNI and NSNI particles whose smoothing domain follows the deformation gradient (the update DeformationGradient, with which the smoothing domain is the particle) take their face loads (addPressure()). The SDI particle (DisplacementParticleSQCNIxSDI::computeDistributedLoad()) and the gradient-enhanced particle with another update of its smoothing domain (GradientEnhancedFiniteStrainParticleSQCNI::faceQuadratureIntermediate()) integrate a pressure at a face center of their own, which does not balance a uniform stress exactly. Section is meant as for finite elements (plane strain, 3D, axisymmetric): the form of the integrals depends on it; in the Cartesian section the integrals carry the weight 1. The class holds static functions only, so that a particle selects its integrals with its own template parameters.
